COMPONENT: Small rough stone infill patch to the right of the large central-right window, excluding dressed surround and brick. Building-level association; no new OSM footprint match.

Full reference copied unchanged. Crop and trace overlay are adaptations; credit Jeangagnon / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0, cropped and annotated for SITU. These reference adaptations retain CC BY-SA 3.0. No source pixels are used in the authored base colour.

WHAT CHANGED
The earlier GTM05 repeatable procedural wall remains available. This is a separate, unique panel with manually interpreted face boundaries from an actual 245 x 250 pixel patch. Review the numbered trace overlay: boundaries are approximate and some fragmentary stones are omitted. Output is 1024 square for editing, not 1024 pixels of recovered photographic detail. Perspective is not metrically rectified. Do not mix this set with earlier maps.

MAPS AND IMPORT
All ten maps share the traced geometry. Base colour: sRGB, authored grey palette, not calibrated albedo. Other channels: linear/non-colour. Height: normalized 16-bit, authored 6 mm range. Normal: choose OpenGL +Y or DirectX -Y; use only one. Roughness .84 stone/.93 mortar is assumed. Metallic and transmission zero; opacity white. AO white is a neutral placeholder. Feature mask marks joints/bevels. Microrelief is authored, not measured from brightness.
NOT TILEABLE. Use a single panel with UVs 0-1 and clamp addressing; no repeating-wall claim. One metre square is an arbitrary test extent, not measured. Avoid combining normal and height bump for the same relief. Displacement stays off. Surface profiles, chemistry, friction and acoustics are not established.

BENCHMARK STATUS
This tests traceability and shader behaviour, not documentary realism. Source age does not verify 2026 condition and does not define a historical-era reconstruction. Better frontal, scale-controlled photographs remain necessary for high-fidelity close-ups.
